PullRequest.Title: sessions: Preserve focus during background session replacement
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Fix the focus race behind intermittent WSL Dev Container smoke timeouts, with follow-up diagnostics and cancellation-safe Windows CI log publication.

- Sample focus ownership before replacing a session: restore composer focus only when the replaced session view owned it. Otherwise preserve focus in Quick Input or another surface.
- Publish the replacement's focus intent atomically with the active session. Preserve normal explicit navigation.
- Add regression coverage for external focus, focused-composer replacement, explicit navigation, and atomic focus intent.
- Print bounded, redacted WSL picker/focus/notification and renderer/shared-process diagnostics to smoke task output while preserving the original failure.
- Publish Windows diagnostic logs and stop lingering test processes even on cancellation. Allow ten minutes for cancellation cleanup/publication; normal job and picker timeouts are unchanged.

## Reproduction

Investigating [Azure build 474825](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=474825&view=logs&j=15ec5277-fdc6-550c-b203-acb65f44f31c&t=19c87eee-4f28-5155-a71e-4ac992305659&s=27eddb93-7805-576c-c80f-37b2176e40f7), a normal local repetition reproduced the picker timeout. Temporary focus instrumentation then captured background draft recreation calling `focusSession` while **Connect via WSL** was visible, dismissing the picker on blur before any WSL host connection started.

The original Azure attempt also hit its job timeout during post-test scanning, which skipped log publication and lost its screenshot/trace. The cancellation changes address that separate diagnostics gap.

## Validation

- Regression test failed before the fix and passes afterward.
- Focused session suites after rebase: **229 passing, 2 pending**.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, client transpilation, smoke/automation compilation, scoped hygiene, and whitespace checks passed.
- Real WSL Dev Container UI smoke: **three consecutive passes before rebase, plus another pass after rebasing onto `origin/main`**.
- Injected WSL startup failure verified diagnostic output, token redaction, and preservation of the original timeout; temporary instrumentation removed.
- Azure YAML parsed locally. Cancellation-time artifact publication has **not yet been exercised in CI**.

Follow-up to #336573. This branch contains one new commit on top of `origin/main`.

Scenarios.Scenario: An active draft or provider session is replaced while focus remains inside that session's composer.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The provider's synchronous replacement event flows through SessionsManagementService to SessionsService._onDidReplaceSession, performs two slot lookups, replaces the visible wrapper transactionally, reruns the renderer reconciliation, and restores composer focus. The focus call performs two getBoundingClientRect reads and may scroll the view before focusing it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the active DOM element, perform two geometry reads, optionally scroll the active SessionView, and focus its composer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One focus-detection scan per replacement; geometry/focus occurs once only when the replaced mounted view owned focus. Each scan is over V mounted slots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Different-ID active replacements already triggered focus and geometry work regardless of external focus; same-ID replacements did not refocus because the guard compared IDs. The diff adds refocus only for same-ID replacements whose old view actually owned focus, while suppressing focus for externally focused replacements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on the replacement event path, but bounded to a single lifecycle event and a small visible-slot set.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One replacement per draft graduation/provider replacement, multiplied by the number of visible session slots V. getSessionView, getFocusedSessionView, renderer active-slot lookup, and focusSession each scan at most V mounted slots; V is the user-visible grid cardinality rather than the full session catalog.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Replacement listeners and observable reconciliation execute synchronously and serially on the renderer thread; there is no parallel work or queue burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Mounted SessionView slots are reused by SessionsPart. Lookups are uncached linear scans over the small mounted slot set; the wrapper is intentionally recreated once for the replacement. No cold/warm network, filesystem, or process cache is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event path, linear slot scans, identity guard, and geometry reads are directly traced. They do not form a realistic hot or scaling regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact visible-slot counts and browser layout cost vary, but replacement frequency is lifecycle-bounded and tests establish the focus call occurs at most once per replacement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added same-ID focus restoration is one bounded UI operation when focus was already in the replaced composer, while the new focus test removes previously unnecessary focus work when another surface owns focus.

Scenarios.Scenario: A WSL Dev Container smoke connection proceeds successfully.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The automation invokes the existing command, waits for one of two Quick Input pickers, selects the distribution/folder, and continues through the existing WSL and Dev Container setup. The diff adds only synchronous logger messages around existing waits and selections; diagnostic capture is not reached.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing Playwright/automation commands query and manipulate Quick Input in the renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged constant sequence per connection attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command, picker waits, visibility check, clicks, and folder selection occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing picker waits and UI interactions remain on the connection critical path; added logger calls are negligible.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One WSL connection attempt per configured smoke scenario, with a constant number of added log records.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing automation remains sequential; no new promise fan-out, subprocess, filesystem, network, or IPC concurrency is added on success.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or retry behavior. Existing WSL fixture subprocess/network setup is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the success path is directly visible and does not invoke the new diagnostic methods.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Logger sink implementation cost is not measured, but only five short records are added per WSL connection.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The normal connection critical path gains only constant-size logging and no expensive boundary or multiplicity change.

Scenarios.Scenario: A WSL Dev Container smoke scenario fails and emits connection diagnostics before preserving the original failure.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the scenario has already failed, automation evaluates a bounded DOM snapshot, then the fixture enumerates the suite log directory and serially reads the shared-process log plus one renderer log per window, capped at 256 KiB each, filters to the last 20 matching entries, redacts/output-caps entries, and then runs the pre-existing broader failure diagnostics before rethrowing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Evaluate renderer DOM state and serialize the bounded snapshot to the smoke runner.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request after a WSL fixture-backed scenario failure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No WSL-specific UI snapshot was requested before the existing generic failure diagnostics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the successful product path but on failure completion/reporting before the test rethrows.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate suite window directories and read the tail of sharedprocess.log and each window renderer.log.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: W+1 serial reads, each capped at 256 KiB; realistic smoke runs use one or a few windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The WSL-specific renderer/shared-process tails were not read; the existing subsequent dumpFailureDiagnostics already enumerated windows and read other failure logs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded I/O before failure reporting completes, after the scenario is already failed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: W+1 log files where W is the number of windowN directories in one isolated smoke suite; at most 256 KiB is read per file, 20 matching entries retained per file, and individual emitted entries are sliced to 2,000 characters. UI collections are capped at 5 quick inputs, 10 rows each, 10 notifications, and 5 dialogs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM evaluation is one automation IPC request. Files are opened/read/closed serially in a for loop, so there is no I/O burst; errors are handled per file and diagnostic work completes before the original error is rethrown.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used because this is a one-shot failure snapshot. Each selected file is read once from its tail; no negative-cache behavior or retries are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: call placement, file cardinality, byte caps, serial scheduling, and output caps are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A pathological suite with many window directories increases serial reads linearly, and slow filesystem duration is unmeasured, but suite isolation and the per-file cap keep realistic cost bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The new work is failure-only diagnostic I/O with concrete byte and output bounds, not a product hot path or an uncontrolled fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: A Windows Azure product/CI test job is canceled while tests or test processes are still active.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Azure now grants a ten-minute cancellation phase. The always-conditioned cleanup performs one WMI process enumeration and force-stops matching test-root processes, after which the 1ES pipeline output publishes the .build/logs artifact on cancellation as it already did on success/failure.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query Win32_Process through CIM and force-stop lingering test-root processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One WMI enumeration plus up to P Stop-Process calls for P lingering test processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The step ran on success or failure but was skipped once the job was canceled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs only during the newly allowed cancellation cleanup phase and helps release log handles before publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One artifact publication per affected job, including canceled jobs after this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Log publication ran on success/failure and was skipped on cancellation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extends cancellation completion and agent occupancy, but only within the explicit ten-minute cancellation budget and preserves diagnostics that cancellation previously lost.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One process query per canceled job, stop calls proportional to lingering test processes under the test root, and one log artifact whose bytes scale with that job's generated logs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Pipeline steps and output publication are sequenced during cancellation; cleanup does not create a concurrent process burst. The phase is globally bounded by cancelTimeoutInMinutes: 10.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No caches. Publication transfers the current job log tree once; canceled jobs previously skipped these cancellation-only operations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: conditions and cancellation budget directly establish the added cancellation-only process and network work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of canceled jobs, lingering processes, log bytes, and upload duration are not established. The worst scheduling extension is explicitly bounded at ten minutes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This is an intentional, bounded cancellation scheduling tradeoff needed to terminate holders and preserve failure diagnostics; there is no evidence of disproportionate cardinality or work on normal builds.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 11 changed files and every diff hunk for the performance focus. Traced active-session replacement through observable reconciliation and DOM focus, WSL smoke success/failure diagnostics through automation IPC and bounded filesystem reads, and Windows cancellation cleanup through process enumeration and artifact publication. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not establish a shipped performance-regression fix requiring blame.
